summary: Signed-URL + header normalization causing per-route rate-accounting mismatch and 429s
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports a spike of 429 responses originating after they enabled signed URL uploads through a CDN + custom WAF. The pattern is persistent for a subset of requests that include dynamically-injected headers (Accept-Language and X-Client-Geo).

Impact: LuminaHealth is seeing ~15% of ingest requests return 429s intermittently for 3k-6k requests/min burst windows. This impacts nightly patient-data sync jobs (bulk embedding) and some live web callbacks. Customer reports retries are not smoothing out errors because retries are routed to different edge proxies and still hit 429s.

Environment: prod-us-east (private VPC). Dedicated pool with reserved capacity; traffic goes through customer CDN and an upstream WAF that rewrites/injects headers. Model endpoints affected: gpt-3.8-xl ingestion route used by the embed pipeline.

Steps to reproduce (from customer):
1) Use signed upload URLs through their CDN edge (signed-url validity 10m).
2) Client performs parallel multipart POSTs (~50 concurrent connections).
3) CDN injects X-Client-Geo header per request and rewrites Accept-Language for localization edge optimization.
4) Requests arrive at our edge layer and intermittently receive 429 with Retry-After.

Observed behavior: 429s correlate with a change in the request fingerprint used by our rate-accounting layer. When headers vary per connection (Accept-Language or X-Client-Geo), some requests are getting routed to a different per-route bucket than expected which exhausts the smaller per-path quota and produces 429. Console shows tenant quota appears healthy overall but per-route counters spike.

Expected behavior: Signed-url multipart uploads should be accounted against the tenant/bulk-ingest pool and not split unexpectedly across route-specific buckets due to header variance. Normal operation should allow concurrency up to the reserved capacity without soft-throttling.

Logs / traces / evidence:
- Sample trace IDs: 0f4a1b7e-3c4f-4d9a-9f2e-71b2c9a6b0ab, 1c8b2f42-7d9b-4a3c-93d2-6f4e12e6a9d4
- Edge logs show differing normalized_path values when Accept-Language is present: "/v1/embeds?path=upload&locale=en-US" vs "/v1/embeds?path=upload" which leads to separate route accounting.
- Rate-limiter diagnostics (from edge sidecar) show small per-path windows hit 100% when header-injected variants increase.
- Customer provided a short pcap showing the CDN adds X-Client-Geo per request and occasionally includes a random suffix in Accept-Language for experimentation (e.g., "en-US-r1").

Initial hypothesis: The rate-accounting fingerprint includes normalized path + selected headers. Upstream header mutations are creating multiple distinct fingerprints so the request fanout is split into many small buckets, exhausting some and returning 429s even though tenant-level pool is available. This is a misalignment between our path normalization and the customer's CDN header rewriting.

Immediate business risk: Continued 429s during nightly sync will cause prolonged retries and increased cost for the customer and may trigger SLA credits. Customer requested a mitigation before their next nightly window (scheduled 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC).

Requested action: Ask Edge/Rate-limiter team to confirm which headers are used in route fingerprinting, provide a quick mitigation (ignore certain headers for fingerprinting or collapse locale variants), and advise configuration guidance for customers using signed URLs + CDN.
comments: 2026-03-12 09:15 - Sophie Martinez (Support): Opened ticket after LuminaHealth escalated via enterprise SLA channel. Attached sample traces and a short pcap. Customer is on a private deployment and requested urgent mitigation before nightly sync.

2026-03-12 11:02 - Ethan Cole (SRE): Acknowledged. Reproduced basic symptom locally by replaying sample with varied Accept-Language headers. Observed per-path counters diverging when Accept-Language not stripped during path normalization. Adding Edge@api-gateway to components.
Action: instrument rate-limiter to dump chosen fingerprint components for problematic traces.

2026-03-12 14:30 - Priya Nair (Edge): Confirmed edge code currently includes 'Accept-Language' and 'X-Client-Geo' in fingerprint for route sharding when present. That was intended for A/B routing but causes over-sharding for signed URLs.
Mitigation: propose a conservative change to exclude Accept-Language from fingerprint for the /v1/embeds upload path; X-Client-Geo still useful for geo routing but we can whitelist values instead of using raw header string. Preparing a small config toggle for canary deploy.

2026-03-12 18:05 - Sophie Martinez (Support): Sent mitigation plan to customer. LuminaHealth approves a config toggle for their org to ignore Accept-Language in path fingerprinting for the uploads route. They prefer a per-org toggle over global change.

2026-03-13 02:10 - Ethan Cole (SRE): Deployed canary toggle to edge for LuminaHealth's org-id in us-east. Monitored for one hour over the same ingest pattern; per-path counters collapsed to expected aggregate and 429s dropped from ~15% to <1% in the sample window. No service impact observed.
Next: schedule a rollout to prod for LuminaHealth and create runbook entry to recommend customers strip or stabilize dynamic headers when using signed URLs + CDN.

2026-03-14 08:22 - Sophie Martinez (Support): Customer confirmed nightly sync at 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC completed successfully and error rates returned to baseline. LuminaHealth requested documentation explaining best practices for signed-URL workflows and header behavior.

2026-03-14 12:00 - Priya Nair (Edge): Follow-up: opened PR to add per-org fingerprint config and a safe-default to exclude Accept-Language variants for known upload routes. PR: https://github.com/redwood/reverse-proxy/pull/478. Added confluence runbook link for operations guidance.
resolution: Mitigated: Applied per-org canary toggle to ignore Accept-Language in route fingerprinting for LuminaHealth in prod-us-east. 429s dropped to baseline. Long-term fix: PR to add per-route header whitelist and per-org fingerprint config merged and scheduled for controlled rollout. Recommended customer guidance: normalize headers at CDN or use a stable Accept-Language value for signed-url flows. Follow-up action: create an outbound KB article and add example config for private VPC customers.
